title: add interactive onboarding checkpoints and automatic release summarizer for model profiles
author: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Motivation: New model onboarding flows frequently omit contextual metadata (intended task, expected token lengths, eval prompts) and lightweight perf signals. This causes noisy profiles and brittle release notes. This PR introduces an interactive checkpoint system that collects curated metadata, runs a short profiling harness, validates semantic versioning for variants, and emits a human-friendly draft release summary for maintainers to review.

What this PR does (summary): Adds an interactive CLI and web-backed checkpoint protocol to the registry onboarding flow, a compact profiling harness that runs 2-3 representative payloads, a checkpoint schema + validation rules (required keys, recommended keys, value ranges), an auto-generated release note summarizer that consumes the checkpoint and profiling outputs to propose release note bullet points, and wiring to persist checkpoints as first-class objects in the registry DB.

Design notes: Checkpoints are intentionally small and immutable once persisted (append-only). Each checkpoint contains: model_metadata (name, architecture, dataset hints), perf_snapshot (latency P50/P95 for short samples, median token/sec), sample_prompts (2–3 canonical prompts), and compatibility_tags (quantized/float16/kv_cache_compatible). The summarizer uses heuristics (change-type detection, quantization detection, perf delta thresholds) to draft a one-paragraph summary and a bulleted changelog suitable for release notes.

Developer-facing changes: - CLI: bin/registry-onboard --interactive will guide authors through checkpoints; non-interactive mode accepts a JSON checkpoint. - Web: small modal in the registry UI that surfaces the same checkpoint flow (React + light UX). - DB: migration 20260218_add_checkpoint_table.sql adds checkpoint table and indexes. - Config: onboarding.checkpoints.required_fields override.

Backward compatibility and safety: Existing onboarders that do not opt-in will continue to work; the CLI is opt-in. Checkpoints are validated server-side; invalid checkpoints fail pre-commit and CI checks. The release summarizer only produces a draft — no automatic publishing.

Testing and validation: Added unit tests for schema validation and summarizer heuristics (tests/onboard/test_checkpoints.py), two integration E2E scenarios that exercise the CLI and the web flow in CI. Local perf harness uses a mocked runtime and a short-run real model against a small GPU pool for sanity checks.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag controlled (onboarding.checkpoints.enabled=false by default). Gradual opt-in with squad-level pilots, then org-wide enablement. Documentation in docs/registry/onboarding.md includes authoring tips and a sample release note.

Checklist: [x] schema + migrations, [x] CLI UX, [x] web UX, [x] perf harness, [x] summarizer heuristics, [x] unit & integration tests, [x] docs, [x] migration notice

review_thread: Marcus: please ensure the schema covers 'expected_input_tokens' — responded and added range validation; Priya: suggested rewording release summary to avoid claims about accuracy — updated summarizer to include a confidence suffix; Liam: requested perf harness be non-flaky in CI — added local mock path and a shorter time budget; Author (Sofia): addressed comments and pushed CI-fix commit to stabilize tests.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash by Marcus Chen on 2026-03-04 after CI stabilized and two approvals. No blocking review comments remain.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in interactive onboarding checkpoint flow and an automatic release note draft generator for model profiles. Includes a compact profiling harness, schema validations, UI modal, CLI flow, and DB migration.
migration_notice: DB migration adds checkpoints table; rolling upgrade safe. Operators should run migrations during a maintenance window for larger registries.
notes_for_oncall: If a checkpoint record fails validation on ingest, the CLI exits with 422 and descriptive errors. The summarizer runs offline and should not affect serving. If CI perf E2E flakes, run scripts/ci/onboard_integration.sh locally to reproduce.
